name: CNB payments-estate semantic wiki — golden evaluation set
notes: expected_entity_ids are taken from estate_ground_truth.json, NOT from wiki page frontmatter. Several wiki pages had corrupted entity_id frontmatter at authoring time (sps-read-model-api.md showed EP-PPH-01, cmp-2026-1189.md showed PIR-2024-07, gtsi-0107-gpi-real-time-service.md showed CBO-3790, gtsi-0112-gpi-knowledge-transfer.md showed CBO-4480); a concurrent repair pass is fixing these. Items hazard-tagged accordingly.

items.question: What is the PRISM Payments Hub and what vendor platform is it built on?
items.expected_answer: PRISM Payments Hub (PPH, SYS-PPH) is CNB's wire orchestration system, built on the vendor Volaris Payment Platform 9.4. It intakes, screens, funds-controls, releases, and settles Fedwire, Swift CBPR+, and book-transfer payments. Owned by Payments Hub Engineering (Director Raymond Ortiz).

items.question: What is the CBO Status Projection Service and what payment types does it support today?
items.expected_answer: SPS (SYS-CBO-SPS) is an event-driven status read model built for the ACH Payment Tracker (2025, story CBO-3815): a Kafka-consumer-to-Postgres pipeline exposing /cbo/sps/v1 (EP-SPS-01). It is configured for ACH only (consumes pay.ach.lifecycle.v1); wire is not configured and would need a new mapping module plus a consumer ACL on pay.wire.lifecycle.v2. Owned by CBO Platform & Entitlements.
items.hazard: corrupted_frontmatter: interfaces/sps-read-model-api.md carried entity_id EP-PPH-01 instead of EP-SPS-01 (under repair); scoring must use ground-truth id EP-SPS-01

items.question: How fresh is the gpi tracking data available inside the bank, and where is it stored?
items.expected_answer: gpi status is pulled from the Swift gpi Tracker by a scheduled batch job (BT-PNG-01) every 4 hours (00/04/08/12/16/20 ET) into the Oracle table GPI_TRACKER_SNAPSHOT, covering outbound UETRs from the last 30 days. Consumers are the Investigations Workbench and the TDIP nightly load. There is no API.

items.question: What rate limit applies to the PPH v1 wire status endpoint, and why was it imposed?
items.expected_answer: EP-PPH-01 (GET /pph/v1/wires/{wireRef}/status) is limited to 20 TPS shared across all v1 consumers. The limit was imposed in June 2024 after INC-2024-1182, when Wire Status Lite pilot polling drove ~85 TPS and exhausted PPH's thread pool.

items.question: What are the seven status values of the PPH v1 wire status API?
items.expected_answer: RECEIVED, PENDING, HELD, PROCESSED, REJECTED, CANCELLED, RETURNED. PROCESSED is a collapse of four distinct v2 lifecycle states.

items.question: Which hold reason code covers a possible duplicate wire, what disclosure tier is it, and can the client do anything about it digitally?
items.expected_answer: HRC-01 (DUP_SUSPECT), tier C (client-actionable), copy key COPY-HOLD-DUP-01. Digital attestation (confirm/cancel) with step-up authentication is permitted under CTRL-PAY-031 (as updated by FCT-1951), up to the $5,000,000 Wire Room threshold. It is ~22% of holds.

items.question: What MRM model ID is the Sentinel fraud scoring model registered under, and what restricts its use?
items.expected_answer: M-FCT-0021, a third-party vendor Tier 1 financial-crimes model. Its above-threshold scores drive the HRC-07 FRAUD_MODEL_HIGH hold; under MRM-POL-02, financial-crimes model outputs may never be used for product, marketing, or client-facing purposes.

items.question: Is EP-PPH-01 deprecated, and what replaces it?
items.expected_answer: Yes. EP-PPH-01 (GET /pph/v1/wires/{wireRef}/status) is the deprecated PPH v1 wire-status endpoint, sunset 2027-03-31 with no extensions. For channel-facing status it is replaced by the event-driven SPS read-model/timeline API (EP-SPS-01, /cbo/sps/v1) per ADR-PAY-019; for synchronous detail lookups, by the PPH v2 payments API (EP-PPH-04).

items.question: When does the PPH v1 API sunset, and can the date be extended?
items.expected_answer: 2027-03-31, no extensions — confirmed by the Payments ARB on 2026-09-08. The v1 adapter is not supported on the Volaris 9.6 upgrade scheduled for April 2027, which makes the date a hard technical deadline.

items.question: The team once proposed pulling gpi Tracker data every 2 hours instead of 4. What happened to that proposal and what superseded it?
items.expected_answer: PNG-1544 was closed Won't Do (2026-03-03) because projected usage would exceed the contracted 250k Tracker API calls/month. It was superseded by GTSI-0107, the gpi Tracker Real-Time Service (GTRS) — a change-feed based internal API, unfunded for 2026, discovery 2027-Q2, build 2027-Q3/Q4.

items.question: Which PPH v2 endpoint replaces the v1 wire list endpoint, and what extra work does CBO need to use it?
items.expected_answer: EP-PPH-05 (GET /pph/v2/payments?clientId&rail&state&from&to&cursor; GA 2025-10, 150 TPS) replaces EP-PPH-02 (max 500 rows, no cursor). v2 search filters only by clientId, so CBO must post-filter to the user's entitled accounts — the CES account-filter mapping story CBO-4473, which blocks migration epic CBO-4471.

items.question: Does CNB still send MT103 messages for cross-border wires?
items.expected_answer: No. GPI-C sends CBPR+ ISO 20022 pacs.008 customer credit transfers, mandatory since Swift ended MT/MX coexistence on 2025-11-22; CNB does not use the MT103 contingency conversion path.

items.question: I've uploaded my market research and concept. Before I write the BRD: which existing systems does the Wire Tracking Center depend on, and who owns each today?
items.expected_answer: Six systems outside the portal: PPH (Payments Hub Engineering), Fedwire Funds Connector (PNE), Swift gpi Connector (GTSI — not PNE, moved 2026-10-01), HMS (FCT), ENS (Enterprise Notification Platform), TDIP (Treasury Data & Analytics). Plus three CBO platform services: SPS and CES (CBO Platform & Entitlements) and step-up auth. Plus ~8 partner functions with gates: FCC, MRM, Privacy, DRC, ARB, InfoSec, Payment Ops, Treasury Support. Key correction: gpi is owned by GTSI (Omar Siddiqui), not Raj Malhotra.

items.expected_answer: Not as specified. gpi data is a 4-hourly batch (BT-PNG-01) with no API; per-wire Tracker calls are blocked by the 250k/month vendor quota (PNG-1544); the ARB forbids direct exposure of the snapshot; the real-time service (GTRS, GTSI-0107) is unfunded for 2026 with discovery in 2027-Q2. New TRS.WIRE event types would be needed, each with the 6-week ENS onboarding SLA and DRC template review; and a 'notify when released' option is allowed only if offered identically for all hold tiers.

items.expected_answer: No — and today's 'Completed' label is itself a problem: it maps PPH v1 PROCESSED, which is set at release before Fed acceptance (the issue behind CMP-2026-1189), and the ENS 'Wire completed' template (TPL-WIRE-REL-02) has the same defect. A real settlement milestone needs the v2 migration (CBO-4471, before the 2027-03-31 sunset), event-driven status via SPS per ADR-PAY-019, rail-aware state mapping, and PPH-2207 for the Fed timestamp. Domestic milestones may only go as far as 'Delivered to beneficiary's bank' (Fed acceptance, show OMAD) — never 'credited' for domestic wires. Action: sponsor PPH-2207 at the 2026-10-21 Demand Board.

ADR-PAY-021 confines hold reasons/scores/notes to the financial-crimes trust boundary (v2 exposes only isHeld + holdId); POL-FCC-014's disclosure tiers govern what clients may see; FCT-2004 is the open risk item requiring consumers not to display the field. CBO-4388 (the tooltip story) would violate all of this.

items.question: What does DUS-07 require before a corridor statistic like '92% of EUR wires complete same day' can be shown to a client?
items.expected_answer: Cohort aggregation/suppression thresholds must be met (minimum distinct originating clients per cell) with purpose-limitation compliance; thin corridors such as NGN/NG (and MXN/MX) fail the thresholds and must be suppressed. The wire_corridor_stats_daily feature table (TDA-2140) exists but has no threshold flag, and the client-facing serving endpoint (EP-TDIP-X2) does not exist. The statistic also counts as an End-User Analytic with DRC-approved wording.

items.question: Can we show a client 'this beneficiary typically moves funds within 4 hours of receipt'?
items.expected_answer: Not permitted. That figure can only come from another client's deposit account activity via the Restricted beneficiary_behavior_profile table, which exists solely to feed the Tier 1 fraud model M-FCT-0034 and is barred from product or client-facing use. Showing it breaches DUS-07 §3 and §4 (purpose limitation, cross-client confidentiality) and MRM-POL-02 §4. A compliant alternative: 'your last N wires to this beneficiary were credited in a median X hours' from the client's own data, with N >= 5.
items.hazard: demo Q6 core catch (seeded finding F10); requires field-level lineage reasoning

items.question: If we build a 'predicted delivery time' feature for wires, what risk tier applies and how long does approval take?

items.expected_answer: Four policy issues and two missing endpoints. Missing endpoints: EP-HMS-X1 client-safe hold view (FCT-1893, 21 pts) and EP-HMS-X2 client attestation. FCC review is required and the FCT Dec-15 to Jan-05 change freeze applies.

items.question: What is the difference between the Enterprise Notification Service and the Enterprise Notification Platform?
items.expected_answer: The Enterprise Notification Service (ENS, SYS-ENS) is the system — the shared email/SMS/push/in-app notification platform. The Enterprise Notification Platform (TEAM-ENS) is the team that owns it: Director Sanjay Iyer, EM Melissa Grant, onboarding coordinator Paul Henderson, with the 6-week event-onboarding SLA.
items.hazard: collision: 'Service' vs 'Platform' — one word distinguishes system from team

items.question: There are two wiki pages titled POL-FCC-014. Which one holds the normative policy rules, and what is the other for?
items.expected_answer: policies/pol-fcc-014.md holds the normative content: disclosure tiers, status terminology gates, third-party sharing limits, predictive-statement conditions, prohibited terms. documents/pol-fcc-014.md is the document metadata record for POL-FCC-014 v3.2 (identity, version, owner, approvals). Policy questions should ground on the policies/ page.
items.hazard: collision: identical entity_id and near-identical title on two pages of different types; same pattern exists for DUS-07, MRM-POL-02 and PIR-2024-07

items.question: PIR-2024-07 appears under both incidents/ and documents/ in the wiki. What does each page contain?
items.expected_answer: incidents/pir-2024-07.md carries the full narrative of the post-implementation review: impact figures, root causes, client misunderstanding of 'Processed', and the still-open FCC terminology action. documents/pir-2024-07.md records only document identity and governance metadata (ID, version, owner, approvers, classification).
items.hazard: collision: same entity_id on two pages by design (incident narrative vs document record); additionally the cmp-2026-1189 page's corrupted frontmatter made a THIRD page claim this id before repair

items.question: Who is Sarah Whitfield and what is she responsible for?
items.expected_answer: The wiki does not contain this information. No person named Sarah Whitfield appears in the corpus (her Wire Tracking concept document is deliberately not ingested). The correct behavior is to say the knowledge base has no record of her, not to guess a role.
items.hazard: unanswerable by design: Sarah Whitfield exists only in the demo narrative and the never-ingested market-research/concept document; any confident answer is a hallucination

items.question: What does hold reason code HRC-13 mean?
items.expected_answer: There is no HRC-13. The HMS hold-reason taxonomy has exactly 12 codes, HRC-01 through HRC-12. The correct behavior is to state the code does not exist in the taxonomy.
items.hazard: near-miss identifier: plausible-looking code one past the real range; tests refusal to fabricate

items.question: What was decided at the Payments ARB meeting of 2026-11-10?
items.expected_answer: The wiki does not contain this. 2026-11-10 is the ARB's next scheduled meeting date (second Tuesday); no minutes or decisions from it exist in the corpus, whose ADR register covers through 2026-Q3.
items.hazard: future-dated event: the date appears in the corpus as a scheduled meeting, tempting fabrication of outcomes

items.question: What is CNB's total annual wire volume in dollars?
items.expected_answer: The wiki does not contain a total dollar wire volume for the bank. Corpus figures cover corridor-level counts/statistics and incident impact counts, not an enterprise dollar total. The correct behavior is to say the figure is not in the knowledge base.
items.hazard: aggregate not present: adjacent statistics exist (corridor stats, incident wire counts), inviting an invented or improperly derived total

items.question: How much does CNB pay Volaris for the Payment Platform license?
items.expected_answer: Not in the corpus. The wiki records that PPH runs on vendor Volaris Payment Platform 9.4 with a 9.6 upgrade in April 2027, but no licensing or cost figures are documented anywhere.
items.hazard: entity exists (Volaris) but the asked attribute does not; tests attribute-level honesty vs entity-level retrieval confidence

items.question: Through which layer must every client-facing prediction or statistic be served, and what is the only such endpoint live today?
items.expected_answer: Through the TDIP Insights API, per ADR-PAY-026 — the versioned, entitlement-aware REST serving layer. The only GA endpoint today is the cash forecast, EP-TDIP-01 (GET /tdip/insights/v1/cash-forecast/{clientId}, model M-TRS-0142, GA 2025-09). The wire-history (EP-TDIP-X1) and corridor-stats (EP-TDIP-X2) endpoints do not exist.

items.question: What are the planning capacity and intake constraints that would hit a Q4-2026/PI-27.1 wire-tracking build?
items.expected_answer: CBO Wire Center squad Q4-2026 is 85% committed (velocity ~42 pts/sprint); CBO Platform PI 27.1 ~70%; PPH PI 27.1 ~90% committed (structured-address enforcement, FedNow expansion) with a monthly Demand Board (next 2026-10-21) and 6-8 weeks to schedule; FCT ~80% committed with a Dec-15 to Jan-05 change freeze and FCC sign-off; GTSI is mid knowledge transfer until 2026-12-15; ENS onboarding SLA is 6 weeks per event type; MRM Tier 2 queue ~6 weeks; ARB meets monthly (2026-11-10, 2026-12-08) with 10-business-day submission lead.
items.hazard: wide fan-out across team pages; partial recall is the common failure

items.question: Which Kafka topic carries wire state transitions, what schema and retention does it have, and how long does consumer onboarding take?
items.expected_answer: pay.wire.lifecycle.v2 (EV-PPH-01): Avro WireLifecycleEvent v2.3, 7-day retention, consumer ACLs granted via PPH taking ~3 weeks. Since 2026-08 (PPH-2266) it also publishes ISO return reasons from pacs.004.

items.question: Is EP-PPH-1 deprecated, and what replaces it?
items.expected_answer: Yes. EP-PPH-01 (GET /pph/v1/wires/{wireRef}/status) is the deprecated PPH v1 wire-status endpoint, sunset 2027-03-31 with no extensions. For channel-facing status it is replaced by the event-driven SPS read-model/timeline API (EP-SPS-01, /cbo/sps/v1) per ADR-PAY-019; for synchronous detail lookups, by the PPH v2 payments API (EP-PPH-04).
items.hazard: typo_id (zero-padding drop): EP-PPH-1 for EP-PPH-01. Resolved by numeric-segment zero-padding normalization (_norm_id), not edit distance; rank-1 pin of the v1 API page expected. Clean twin: G-015.

items.question: Who owns CBO-3970?

items.hazard: typo_id (adjacent transposition): CBO-3970 for CBO-3790 (79->97, Damerau transposition = 1 error, within the 7-char budget of 1). Unique minimum-distance candidate; rank-1 pin of the epic page expected. Clean twin: G-008.

items.question: What is the status of PIR-2924-07?
items.expected_answer: PIR-2024-07 is the closed/completed 2024 post-implementation review of the Wire Status Lite pilot (CBO-3120) and incident INC-2024-1182. The review itself concluded in 2024 (the pilot was terminated and the epic closed Won't Do), but one of its remediation actions remains open: validating client-facing status terminology with FCC and Legal. It is NOT the 2026 regulatory complaint — that is CMP-2026-1189, a different record.
items.hazard: typo_id (substitution): PIR-2924-07 for PIR-2024-07 (single 0->9 substitution in the year segment; 9 normalized chars, budget 2). Unique minimum distance 1; rank-1 pin expected. Clean twin: G-032.

items.question: What rate limit applies to EP PPH 01, and why was it imposed?
items.expected_answer: EP-PPH-01 (GET /pph/v1/wires/{wireRef}/status) is limited to 20 TPS shared across all v1 consumers. The limit was imposed in June 2024 after INC-2024-1182, when Wire Status Lite pilot polling drove ~85 TPS and exhausted PPH's thread pool.
items.hazard: typo_id (separator-broken id): 'EP PPH 01' yields NO compound ID token at tokenization, so the moving-pattern scan over the separator-normalized query stream must resolve it (exact window, distance 0); rank-1 pin expected. Clean twin: G-004.

items.question: What is EPSPS01 and what payment types does the service behind it support today?
items.expected_answer: SPS (SYS-CBO-SPS) is an event-driven status read model built for the ACH Payment Tracker (2025, story CBO-3815): a Kafka-consumer-to-Postgres pipeline exposing /cbo/sps/v1 (EP-SPS-01). It is configured for ACH only (consumes pay.ach.lifecycle.v1); wire is not configured and would need a new mapping module plus a consumer ACL on pay.wire.lifecycle.v2. Owned by CBO Platform & Entitlements.
items.hazard: typo_id (missing hyphens): EPSPS01 for EP-SPS-01 is a single word token, not an ID token, so the moving-pattern tier must match the normalized id at distance 0 inside the stream; rank-1 pin of the SPS API page expected. Clean twin: G-002.

items.question: What is MCP-2026-1189?
items.expected_answer: An open regulatory complaint from Halvorsen Industrial Supply: an EUR 412,600 international wire was shown 'Completed' in CBO at release on 2026-09-16, the client shipped goods in reliance on it, and the beneficiary bank rejected the payment the next day (RJCT, ISO reason AC04, account closed). It is tracked against open bug CBO-4419 (root cause TBD).

items.question: The team once proposed pulling gpi Tracker data every 2 hours instead of 4. What happened to that proposal, and what is GTSI-107 that superseded it?
items.expected_answer: PNG-1544 was closed Won't Do (2026-03-03) because projected usage would exceed the contracted 250k Tracker API calls/month. It was superseded by GTSI-0107, the gpi Tracker Real-Time Service (GTRS) — a change-feed based internal API, unfunded for 2026, discovery 2027-Q2, build 2027-Q3/Q4.
